name: Dominica
title: Holidays in Dominica
intro: Waterfalls, hot springs and resident sperm whales on the Caribbean's wildest island. Here's what Dominica is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: February to April is driest, the trails are less muddy and whale sightings are good. Dominica is a rainforest island, so expect showers at any time of year. The hurricane season runs from June to November, with August to October the riskiest.

things.name: Trafalgar Falls
things.blurb: Twin waterfalls a short walk from the car park, with warm springs nearby to sit in.

things.name: Champagne Reef
things.blurb: Snorkel through streams of warm volcanic bubbles rising from the seabed.

things.name: Whale watching
things.blurb: Sperm whales live off the west coast all year, so sightings are common.

things.name: Titou Gorge
things.blurb: Swim through a narrow, shaded gorge to a small waterfall. Good for confident swimmers.

things.name: Emerald Pool
things.blurb: An easy rainforest trail to a waterfall and green pool, suitable for younger children.

things.name: Kalinago Territory
things.blurb: Meet the Kalinago people, the island's first inhabitants, and see traditional crafts and canoe building.

faqs.question: Is Dominica good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes, for active families who love nature more than beaches. The hiking, river swims and whale trips are excellent. There are few sandy beaches and no big resorts, and the roads are steep and twisty.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: A week covers the main falls, reefs and a whale trip. Ten days lets you slow down or add a longer hike.

faqs.question: How do you get there from the UK?
faqs.answer: There are no direct flights. Most families fly to Antigua or Barbados and connect on a short regional flight, or take the ferry from Guadeloupe or Martinique. British passport holders don't need a visa.

faqs.question: Can children do the Boiling Lake hike?
faqs.answer: It is a tough full-day hike over steep, muddy ground and needs a guide. It suits fit teenagers, but younger children will be happier at Trafalgar Falls or the Emerald Pool.
